rationale: Measured clean: band_low 0.9, crest 20.6 (already controlled), 63 Hz peak, scooped 100-200. HPF 30 removes sub-25 rumble while keeping the 31.5 Hz sub. No tonal EQ needed; warmth/glue comes at the bus.

Body @160-200; 250-400 is already ~10 dB below the 200 Hz peak (NOT honky), so no de-box (a cut there only thinned/brightened it). suppress_resonances was a no-op (no narrow resonance — it's broadband presence), dropped. HPF 70 cleans <125 rumble/bleed while keeping body; the bus (bell -1.5 @2.5k, HS -4 @6k, +1.5 @180, tape) owns the snare's warm tonal shaping.

Hottest stem; strong 63 Hz kick bleed + honky 315-400 peak. HPF 110 trims the deepest bleed/rumble (kick & OH now phase-aligned so residual lows reinforce rather than comb); -2 @400 de-honks. No per-stem de-harsh: cymbals already roll off and the bus HS -4 @6k + Studer tape own the top.
Broadband mids, 400 Hz peak, 63 Hz bleed. HPF 120 cleans rumble; -1.5 @400 keeps it from piling on the OH/snare 400 buildup. Otherwise left as warmth/glue.
